newsitem.title: FRANCE: Air Algerie Paris flights may resume soon.
newsitem.headline: Air Algerie Paris flights may resume soon.

text.p: French aviation officials predicted on Thursday that Air Algerie flights between Algiers and Paris, dropped by the airline in June 1995 in a dispute over safety, would resume before the start of the peak summer season.
"We all hope that Air Algerie and the Paris airports authority can conclude an agreement to resume the flights before the summer season," a Transport Ministry official told Reuters.

France's ties with Algiers, its former colony, were badly frayed by the December 1994 hijacking of an Air France jet in Algeria and by a wave of 1995 bombing attacks claimed by fundamentalist rebels unhappy with Paris' support for the army-backed Algerian authorities.
Investigators also suspect Algerian rebels in the December 3 rush-hour bombing of a Paris commuter train in which four people died, though no one has claimed responsibility for that bombing.

All French airlines cancelled their services to Algeria for security reasons after the Christmas Eve 1994 hijacking, leaving Air Algerie as the only company currently flying between France and Algeria, serving the French cities of Lyon and Marseille.

But it cancelled its service to Paris in June 1995 after French authorities insisted on transferring its operations to an isolated high-security terminal at Roissy-Charles de Gaulle airport to the north of Paris, from Orly to the city's south.
In a diplomatic spat reflecting the weakened ties between the two states, Air Algerie complained the new facilities discriminated against its passengers.

France has since agreed to move Air Algerie's Paris-Algiers flights to a regular terminal at Charles de Gaulle, and Air Algerie officials are mulling as many as six round-trips a day between the two capitals, French officials said.
"The airline's demands are under study, and appear headed for a favourable conclusion," said the French ministry official, who spoke on condition of anonymity.
Air Algerie officials could not immediately be reached for comment.
